decisions.reason: Confirmed missing inference: the atlas and diagonal criterion applies only to a stack in groupoids. New step 1.3 descends affine torsors, their actions and equivariant maps using effective affine algebra descent and represented-morphism descent; identities and unique gluing establish both stack axioms. The Statement, atlas and affine diagonal are unchanged, including empty X and rank-zero factors.

The rejection overlooks the supplier proof: cover-small theorem steps 1.1–4.1 construct image-nonenlarging subdivision/prism operators, simplex-dependent depths, R=1-dD-Dd, and D=0 on small chains. Hence R,D preserve both open-set subcomplexes and D contracts J=C(L)/N. Extending that contraction across the remaining simplex basis gives T=1-de-ed, the chain inverse used in step 3.2. No CW-pair assumption is made for the open complements.

No circular inference: the definition specifies the group H_(i+2g)^(BM,G)(X) and the induced-presentation convention, using only the published variety-normalized supplier. Substitution into its finite-stage index j+2(t-g) gives i+2t, and for smooth X the degree is 2(x-g)-i. The later lemma uses precisely these formulas to prove their presentation comparison, not a comparison assumed by the definition; justified_by is the schema-prescribed direction for this deferred well-definedness result.

The relative scheme-level Plucker embedding used in step 1.2 was not established by the cited set definition and full-flag statement. Added the existing Plucker-equation and affine-chart suppliers and proved locally over arbitrary C-algebras that their equations have polynomial pivot charts representing direct-summand subbundles. These charts glue functorially to the closed relative embedding, so arrow invariance is a closed incidence condition and every scheme base change of p is proper. Also made parabolic-torsor descent explicit and included the projective-bundle supplier in inherited AC. The dimension calculation e-u and Statement are unchanged.

F1 wrongly attributes arbitrary-flag geometry to two-block suppliers, although step 1.1 already contains its own adapted-frame construction. This is a nonfatal attribution defect. F1 now distinguishes the two-block conventions and relative Grassmannian construction from the local arbitrary-flag proof. Step 1.1 explicitly realizes flags and preserved-arrow loci as closed incidence varieties, realizes G/L as the open direct-sum decomposition locus, and gives finite pivot sections. These prove separated quasi-projective finite type, including zero ranks. The common L-frame product comparison has both intrinsic indices pull back to i+2 dim U+2 dim V; growing cohomology gaps and principal-bundle descent give naturality and cocycles without assuming the comparison being proved.

Confirmed a nonfatal assumption-accounting defect: F3 invokes the complete-flag lemma for dimension two, whose Statement expressly assumes AC. A1 now records inheritance through both F2 smoothness/properness and F3 projective flag geometry. AC was already in Given and deps, so no claim is weakened. Matrix multiplication gives c+(mu-lambda)t, relative stack dimension is 1-1=0, and the invariant-line calculations and closed incidence properness remain correct.
